content: Before taking tetracycline, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to other tetracyclines (such as doxycycline or minocycline), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other problems. This medication may cause dizziness. Consuming alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate this effect. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or engaging in activities requiring alertness until you can do so safely. Limit your intake of alcoholic beverages. Tetracycline may reduce the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines, such as the typhoid vaccine. Inform your healthcare provider if you are scheduled to receive any vaccinations. This medication can increase your sensitivity to sunlight. Limit your time in the sun, avoid tanning booths and sunlamps, and use sunscreen and protective clothing when outdoors. Tetracycline should not be used by children under 8 years of age, as it may cause permanent tooth discoloration and other issues. Tooth discoloration has also been reported in older children and young adults. If you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, inform your doctor. You should not become pregnant while using tetracycline, as it may harm an unborn baby. This medication also passes into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription and nonprescription drugs and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This medication may interfere with certain lab tests, potentially causing false test results. In the event of an overdose, if someone has serious symptoms such as passing out or trouble breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. This medication has been prescribed for your current condition only. Do not use it later for another infection unless directed by your doctor. Lab and/or medical tests may be performed while you are taking this medication. Keep all medical and lab appointments. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your usual dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Taking outdated tetracycline can result in serious illness. Take this medication by mouth on an empty stomach (at least 1 hour before or 2 hours after meals) as directed by your doctor, usually 2 or 4 times daily. If stomach upset occurs, consult your doctor about taking it with food. Take each dose with a full glass of water (8 ounces or 240 milliliters) unless otherwise directed. Do not lie down for at least 10 minutes after taking this medication. Take this medication 2 to 3 hours before or after consuming products containing aluminum, calcium, iron, magnesium, zinc, or bismuth subsalicylate. Examples include antacids, quinapril, sucralfate, vitamins/minerals, dairy products (such as milk or yogurt), and calcium-enriched juice. The dosage is based on your medical condition and response to treatment. For optimal effect, take this antibiotic at evenly spaced intervals. Continue taking this medication until the full prescribed amount is finished, even if symptoms disappear after a few days. Common side effects may include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, loss of appetite, mouth sores, black hairy tongue, sore throat, dizziness, headache, or rectal discomfort. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefit to you outweighs the risk of side effects. Tetracycline may rarely cause increased pressure around the brain (intracranial hypertension IH). This risk is higher for women of childbearing age who are overweight or have had IH in the past. If IH develops, it usually resolves after stopping tetracycline; however, there is a chance of permanent vision loss or blindness. This medication may rarely cause a severe intestinal condition due to a bacteria called C. difficile. This condition may occur during treatment or weeks to months after treatment has stopped. Prolonged or repeated use of this medication may result in oral thrush or a new yeast infection (oral or vaginal fungal infection). A very serious allergic reaction to this drug is rare. However, seek immediate medical attention if you notice symptoms of a serious allergic reaction, such as rash, itching/swelling (especially of the face/tongue/throat), severe dizziness, or trouble breathing. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., call your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. This information is a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that this product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
